title: PagerRoute
problem_statement: Mid-size SaaS engineering teams of 10–50 engineers lose 4–6 hours per major incident because PagerDuty and CloudWatch alerts land on generic on-call rotations instead of the engineer who owns the affected service. Existing solutions require weeks of configuration and a dedicated SRE function that teams under 50 engineers cannot staff or afford. As incidents cascade, engineers waste time waking colleagues and hunting runbooks scattered across Confluence and Slack, compounding MTTR and eroding team trust. The explosion of microservice architectures among growth-stage SaaS companies makes this problem materially worse each year without a lightweight, low-setup alternative.
target_users: Engineering manager at a 10–50 person SaaS company owning on-call policy without a dedicated SRE team
On-call software engineer who owns one or more microservices and receives misdirected pages
CTO or VP Engineering at a growth-stage SaaS company responsible for incident response KPIs and tooling budget
DevOps or platform engineer tasked with wiring alerts to PagerDuty and maintaining service ownership records
user_stories: As an engineering manager at a 10–50 person SaaS company owning on-call policy without a dedicated SRE team, I want to import our existing service catalog from a YAML file or GitHub CODEOWNERS so that I can define service ownership in under 30 minutes without rebuilding metadata from scratch

As an on-call software engineer who owns one or more microservices and receives misdirected pages, I want every PagerDuty incident I receive to include an inline link to the runbook for the affected service so that I can begin remediation immediately without searching Confluence or Slack

As an on-call software engineer who owns one or more microservices and receives misdirected pages, I want alerts for services I do not own to be automatically routed away from me to the correct owner so that I am not woken for incidents I cannot resolve

As a CTO or VP Engineering at a growth-stage SaaS company responsible for incident response KPIs and tooling budget, I want a weekly report showing mean time to acknowledge and mean time to resolve broken down by service and owner so that I can identify routing gaps and justify the tooling investment to the board

As a DevOps or platform engineer tasked with wiring alerts to PagerDuty and maintaining service ownership records, I want PagerRoute to automatically sync service-to-owner mappings to PagerDuty escalation policies via API so that I do not need to manually update PagerDuty whenever team ownership changes

As an engineering manager at a 10–50 person SaaS company owning on-call policy without a dedicated SRE team, I want to receive a Slack notification when an alert is routed to a service that has no declared owner so that I can close ownership gaps before the next incident

As a DevOps or platform engineer tasked with wiring alerts to PagerDuty and maintaining service ownership records, I want PagerRoute to consume CloudWatch alarm ARNs and map them to services using tag-based rules so that I can onboard new AWS services without writing custom Lambda glue code
acceptance_criteria: A user can complete initial setup — connect PagerDuty API key, connect AWS CloudWatch, and define at least one service with an owner — in 30 minutes or less as measured by end-to-end onboarding session timing in user testing

When a CloudWatch alarm fires, PagerRoute routes the resulting PagerDuty incident to the correct owner's escalation policy within 60 seconds of alarm state change, verified by automated integration tests against a staging PagerDuty account

Every routed PagerDuty incident payload includes a 'runbook_url' field populated with the URL stored for that service; if no runbook URL is configured, the field contains a direct link to the service's edit page in PagerRoute prompting the user to add one

When an alert fires for a service with no declared owner, PagerRoute posts a Slack message to a configured channel within 2 minutes identifying the unowned service by name and linking to the ownership configuration page
Service-to-owner mappings exported from PagerRoute as YAML are re-importable without data loss, confirmed by a round-trip import/export test covering at least 50 services
PagerRoute syncs ownership changes to PagerDuty escalation policies within 5 minutes of a save action in the UI, verified by polling the PagerDuty API in automated tests

The weekly incident report is delivered to a configured email address every Monday at 08:00 in the account's configured timezone and contains MTTA and MTTR figures per service accurate to within 1 minute of values calculated directly from PagerDuty API data

The product supports import of GitHub CODEOWNERS file format and correctly maps code path owners to PagerRoute service owners with at least 95% accuracy on a reference CODEOWNERS fixture with 100 entries
PagerRoute does not store AWS credentials; it uses IAM role delegation or customer-managed secrets manager references exclusively, confirmed by a security review checklist prior to GA launch

success_metrics.metric: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) per incident for PagerRoute-routed alerts
success_metrics.baseline: 18 minutes (industry benchmark for teams without automated routing per PagerDuty's 2023 State of Incident Response report)
success_metrics.target: 8 minutes or less within 90 days of customer go-live

success_metrics.metric: Mean time to resolve (MTTR) for major incidents on services managed by PagerRoute
success_metrics.baseline: 4–6 hours self-reported by target customers in discovery interviews
success_metrics.target: 2 hours or less within 90 days of customer go-live

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of fired alerts routed to the correct service owner without manual reassignment
success_metrics.baseline: 0% (all routing manual or based on generic rotation at baseline)
success_metrics.target: 90% correct first-assignment rate within 60 days of go-live

success_metrics.metric: Onboarding time from account creation to first correctly routed alert
success_metrics.baseline: Weeks (competitor PagerDuty advanced routing configuration estimate from customer interviews)
success_metrics.target: 60 minutes or less for a team with an existing service list

success_metrics.metric: Monthly active accounts retained at 90 days post-signup (product retention)
success_metrics.baseline: No historical baseline; comparator SaaS DevOps tools average 55% 90-day retention (Mixpanel 2023 benchmark)
success_metrics.target: 70% 90-day retention among accounts that completed onboarding

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of onboarded services with a runbook URL populated
success_metrics.target: 75% of services have a runbook URL within 30 days of account go-live

risks_open_questions: PagerDuty API rate limits may throttle bulk escalation policy sync for customers with more than 200 services; need to validate rate limit tiers and implement exponential backoff with user-visible sync status

GitHub CODEOWNERS files map file paths to teams, not services; the mapping heuristic from file path to PagerRoute service may be ambiguous for monorepos — what is the fallback when no deterministic match exists?

AWS CloudWatch does not natively tag alarms with a service identifier in a standardized way; customers must apply consistent resource tags, which may require a migration effort — how do we reduce this friction at onboarding?

Customers using OpsGenie, VictorOps, or Grafana OnCall instead of PagerDuty represent addressable market we cannot serve at launch; when do we add a second alerting platform integration and which platform is highest priority?

Service ownership data contains organizational information (who is on-call, what services exist); what are the data residency and privacy requirements for EU-based customers, and do we need GDPR-compliant data processing agreements before selling to them?
If PagerRoute misroutes a critical production alert, customer trust is severely damaged; what is our liability posture and do we need an indemnification clause in the ToS before GA?
Small engineering teams may resist adding another SaaS tool with another login; should we offer SSO (Google, GitHub OAuth) at launch or post-launch, and does its absence block enterprise trials?

Pricing model is undecided: per-seat, per-service, or flat fee — how does each model align incentives with the cost structure (API calls scale with services, not seats) and what do customers anchor on during sales conversations?
out_of_scope: Building a proprietary alerting engine or replacing PagerDuty/CloudWatch as the alert source; PagerRoute is a routing and enrichment layer only
Incident postmortem tooling, timeline reconstruction, or retrospective workflows
Full runbook authoring or hosting within PagerRoute; only runbook URL storage and inline linking are in scope for v1
Support for alerting platforms other than PagerDuty and AWS CloudWatch at initial launch (OpsGenie, VictorOps, Grafana OnCall, Datadog monitors deferred)
Automated remediation or auto-remediation scripts triggered by alerts
On-call schedule creation or rotation management; PagerRoute reads existing PagerDuty schedules but does not replace PagerDuty's scheduling UI
Mobile application; v1 is web-only with Slack as the mobile notification surface
Enterprise SSO (SAML/SCIM) integration deferred to post-GA based on deal blockers observed in sales pipeline
